description: Denied requests, WAF activity, bans, challenges and CAPTCHAs, rate limits, account protection, sensitive data, honeypots and log delivery of Xproxy nodes (shipped with the product, deploy/grafana).

panels.description: Delay, challenge, CAPTCHA and block actions of the account_guard filter by endpoint class; a rising block rate on login is credential stuffing or brute force.
panels.title: Account guard actions

panels.description: Counted failures or requests, blocks placed, distributed campaigns declared and disposable e-mail registrations.
panels.title: Account guard events, blocks and campaigns

panels.description: Address, account and pair blocks currently held by the account guard.
panels.title: Account blocks in force

panels.description: Clients that solved the CAPTCHA tier of the challenge in the last hour.
panels.title: CAPTCHAs passed (1h)

panels.description: Requests or responses refused by the sensitive_data filter in the last hour.
panels.title: Sensitive data blocks (1h)

panels.description: Responses the sensitive_data filter rewrote before the client saw them.
panels.title: Sensitive responses masked (1h)

panels.description: Validated detector matches (cards, personal identity numbers, IBANs, e-mail, tokens, keys, query credentials, custom patterns) in both directions.
panels.title: Sensitive data findings by kind

panels.description: Messages with findings that were logged, masked or blocked, per direction; response findings are the leaks.
panels.title: Sensitive data messages by outcome

panels.description: Refusals per second by listener kind: what "Denied by reason" is for HTTP, for the other protocols. A kind climbing here is a protocol whose policy is being walked.
panels.title: Protocol refusals by kind

panels.description: The twelve busiest reasons, which is what says whether to widen a list or look for an intruder. xproxy_refusals_untracked_total must stay at zero beside it; anything else is a listener kind naming a refusal it could not label.
panels.title: Protocol refusals by reason

panels.description: Upstream answers pointing into a range answer_policy denies: DNS rebinding and cloud metadata endpoints. The name is innocent in every one of these; the address is not. A steady rate on a network that has never seen one is usually an internal zone that needs allow_names.
panels.title: DNS answers screened by where they pointed

panels.description: Queries whose EDNS Client Subnet option was not forwarded (dns.ecs: strip). The cache is keyed by the question alone, so a forwarded per-subnet answer would be served to every client of the listener.
panels.title: DNS client subnet options stripped

panels.description: RFC 7873 DNS cookies. verified is the number of UDP queries whose source address was proved, which is what makes a UDP client security event attributable and bannable. issued climbing with verified flat means clients that ignore the cookie they were handed.
panels.title: DNS cookies

panels.description: stale is answers served past their TTL because the upstream had nothing (RFC 8767): the feature working and an upstream outage at the same time, so check upstream failures beside it. prefetched is entries refreshed before expiry.
panels.title: DNS answers served stale, and entries prefetched

panels.description: Just-in-time access: the grants that exist and what state each is in. pending is the one to watch -- a request nobody has answered is an operator who cannot work, and an approval system that is quietly ignored is worse than none.
panels.title: Access grants by state

panels.description: Sessions a gate listener turned away for want of a grant, by reason: no_grant is nobody asked, grant_pending is nobody approved, grant_expired is a window that closed, grant_wrong_target is a grant for another machine. Beside them, the approvals actually recorded -- uses without approvals means four eyes is off.
panels.title: Access refused, approved and used

panels.description: Where this estate's TLS private keys are held. file is the number an attacker who reads a machine's file system gets; reference means the key comes from a vault or the environment, so what is on the machine is a token that can be revoked; signer means the key never enters the proxy at all. The number to watch going down is file.
panels.title: Private keys by custody

panels.description: Two counts that mean rotation or negotiation has quietly stopped working. stale is references whose source stopped answering: the previous value is still served on purpose, so nothing breaks and nothing rotates either. fips refused is configured key exchange groups and cipher suites the active module will not do, measured at start, so the clients that ask for them cannot handshake.
panels.title: Secrets not refreshing, and algorithms FIPS refuses

panels.description: Every fetch of a network threat feed, by what came back. not_modified is the feed working as intended -- an unchanged feed costs a 304 rather than a download. failed climbing while fetched does not means the list has stopped being current and is still matching: an indicator the publisher withdrew goes on blocking and a new one never arrives.
panels.title: Threat feeds: fetches by outcome

panels.description: Per list, the three numbers that say whether an import is doing anything. entries at 0 is a list that matches nothing while the configuration says it is enforced. age is seconds since the list was last read, so a line that climbs without falling is a policy frozen where it was loaded. skipped is what a structured feed held that this list did not take -- ten thousand skipped behind four entries is either the wrong feed or the wrong kind.
panels.title: Threat lists: entries, age and what was skipped

panels.description: The push factor's outcomes. approved and denied are people answering; failed is the approval service not answering usefully, which fails closed and stops everybody with that factor signing in. throttled is the fatigue bounds refusing an attempt without sending a notification -- it climbing means somebody with a working first factor is trying to buzz a person into approving.
panels.title: Second factor: approvals and the fatigue bounds

panels.description: Authentications by a key held in a security token, and the ones refused for not being one. A move to hardware keys is finished when refused has fallen to nothing and accepted carries the traffic; refusals continuing means somebody still has only a file.
panels.title: SSH keys: tokens against files

panels.description: Behaviour packs loaded from the signed pack directory. Zero means no packs section, or packs.enabled: false.
panels.title: Packs in force

panels.description: Addresses a behaviour pack is quarantining now. Not bans: each expires with the window of the pack that took it, and xproxyctl packs release lifts one. On a plant every one of these is a master the control room has lost, so the number to expect is zero.
panels.title: Held out by a pack

panels.description: A finding is a shape of events from one actor inside one window that a signed pack says is an ATT&CK technique. It is a detection and not necessarily a refusal; the security log line (reason pack_<id>) carries the actor, the signals in order and the protocols.
panels.title: Behaviour pack findings by severity

panels.description: Which packs are firing. xproxyctl packs show <id> says what a pack looked for and where the behaviour was published.
panels.title: Behaviour pack findings by pack

title: Xproxy security
